articleHeadline: Scientists explore the use of sound waves to destroy the virus responsible for the pandemic.
articleSummary: Brazilian researchers from USP São Carlos and UNESP Presidente Prudente report in vitro evidence that diagnostic ultrasound can destabilize and inactivate SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A (H1N1) by mechanical resonance. articleHeadline: Coffee rust: how to monitor the disease at the onset of the rainy season.
articleSummary: Coffee rust (Hemileia vastatrix) monitoring should intensify October–December as rains and humidity rise in the main coffee-producing regions, to reduce defoliation, protect fruit development, and sustain future yields. articleHeadline: Groundbreaking discovery amid the mosquito threat: The reason dengue-vaccinated people are getting sick again has been revealed.
articleSummary: As of 29 October 2026, dengue fever, transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, threatens about 400 million people annually and causes around 40,000 deaths. articleHeadline: Research report: In-hospital costs of tuberculous meningitis in adult
articleSummary: Tuberculous meningitis in adults admitted to the Philippine General Hospital, Manila, Philippines, imposes substantial in-hospital costs. In a retrospective study of 130 admissions (2022–2024), mean billed charges were PHP 202,596 (about USD 3,716 in 2024 values), with a median of PHP 114,743, indicating a skew toward severe, higher-cost cases. Medications comprised about 48% of total charges. In-hospital mortality among those with known outcomes was 40.0% (50/125). A large majority faced catastrophic spending: 89.9% exceeded 10% of mean annual income; 61.2% exceeded 25%; 37.2% exceeded 40%. Reimbursement gaps are substantial: no PhilHealth TB meningitis case rate; nearest rates cover only 12.7–16.5% of mean costs (91.5% of admissions exceed it). Conclusion: need for dedicated reimbursement and stronger financial protection; single-center, billed-charges limitations.
